plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 5.2.17
plan.contextChunk: This figure is part of a worked example asking to find the volume of the solid generated when the region under y = x^2 over [0, 2] is rotated about the line y = -1. The figure contains two linked views. Left (2D): the xy-plane showing the region R bounded above by the parabola y = x^2 and below by the x-axis between x = 0 and x = 2; the axis of revolution y = -1 is drawn as a horizontal red line, with a rotation arrow indicating revolution about it, and a representative washer cross-section at position x is sketched in gray. Right (3D): the resulting solid of revolution shown in perspective, with a visible central hole (from the inner radius of 1) and the parabolic outer surface. The figure illustrates the washer method: at each x, the cross-section is a washer with outer radius x^2 + 1 and inner radius 1, giving area pi((x^2 + 1)^2 - 1^2) = pi(x^4 + 2x^2), and the volume is computed by integrating this expression from 0 to 2.

elements: 2D xy-axes on the left with labeled ticks: y up to 4, x from 0 to 2
blue curve y = f(x) (default x^2) from x=0 to x=2
light blue filled region R under the curve, above y=0, between x=0 and x=2
label 'R' inside the region, labels 'x^2', '0', '2', 'x', 'y' on the 2D plot
horizontal red line y = c (default y = -1) extending rightward — the axis of revolution, labeled 'y = -1'
curved rotation arrow around the red axis line between the 2D plot and the 3D solid
gray washer cross-section standing in the 2D plane at the current sample position x: annulus with outer radius f(x)-c and inner radius 0-c, perpendicular to the red axis

3D solid of revolution on the right: gray translucent surface of revolution of the region about the red axis, axis along the x-direction, with visible cylindrical inner hole of radius |0-c| and parabolic outer profile of radius f(x)+1
matching highlighted washer slice on the 3D solid at the same sample x position
readout of outer radius R(x), inner radius r(x), and washer area π(R²-r²) at the current x

interactions.label: Curve and axis
interactions.teaches: Changing the generating curve or the axis of rotation redraws the region and reshapes both the washer cross-section and the solid, showing that the function and axis together fix the outer radius f(x)-c and inner radius 0-c at every x

interactions.label: Washer position x
interactions.teaches: Sweeping x slides the washer along the axis and reveals how the outer radius grows with f(x) while the inner radius stays constant, so the washer area π(R²-r²) changes with x — the quantity the integral accumulates
Rotating the 3D view lets the learner see down the bore of the solid to confirm the constant-radius hole left by the gap between the region and the axis y = -1

demo_steps.title: Small x — thin washer
demo_steps.narration: At x = 0.2 the curve is near the x-axis, so the outer radius x²+1 ≈ 1.04 barely exceeds the inner radius 1: the washer is a thin ring and contributes little volume.

demo_steps.title: Large x — fat washer
demo_steps.narration: At x = 2 the outer radius is 2²+1 = 5 against the same inner radius 1, giving area π(25-1) = 24π. The 3D slice visibly thickens toward the right end of the solid.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Layout mirrors the source: flat 2D plot on the LEFT (x-axis horizontal, y-axis vertical, x ∈ [0, 2.5], y ∈ [-1.5, 4.5]), red axis line y = c horizontal at y = -1 running from the plot rightward into the solid, rotation arrow midway, 3D solid on the RIGHT lying on its side with its symmetry axis ALONG the x-direction (same red line). Solid spans x ∈ [0, 2] along the axis; outer surface radius = f(x) - c (default x²+1, so radius grows from 1 at the left face to 5 at the right face), inner cylindrical hole radius = 0 - c (default 1) running the full length. World scale: 1 math unit ≈ 0.5 world units, so the solid is ~1 world unit long and ~5 world units in diameter at its big end. Colors: curve blue #2a7fba, region fill light blue #aed6ea (opacity ~0.5), axis line red #c0392b, washer cross-section gray #9aa0a6, solid gray #c8ccd0 translucent (~0.45 opacity) so the hole reads. Washer formula: A(x) = π[(f(x)-c)² - (0-c)²]; default gives π(x⁴+2x²), V = ∫₀² π(x⁴+2x²)dx = 206π/15.
interactionPlan.notes: Build the solid with THREE.LatheGeometry (rotate the profile [(0-c, x), (f(x)-c, x)] about the axis) then re-orient so the lathe axis lies along world X; regenerate geometry reactively when either equation field changes. Guard against f(x) < 0 or axis crossing the region: clamp radii to ≥ 0 and note invalid input inline. The 2D plot is a flat overlay group on the left of the same scene; the washer in the 2D view and the highlighted slice on the 3D solid both track the sweepX slider. Render the solid double-sided with a subtle wireframe or silhouette edge so the hole is legible.

authoredContext: Find the volume of the solid generated when the region under the curve y = x2 over the interval [0, 2] is rotated about the line y =−1. Solution. First sketch the region and the axis of revolution; then imagine revolving the region about the axis (Figure 5.2.17). At each x in the interval 0 ≤ x ≤ 2, the cross section of the solid perpendicular to the axis y =−1 is a washer with outer radius x2 + 1 and inner radius 1. Since the area of this washer is A(x) = π([x2 + 1] 2 − 12 ) = π(x4 + 2x2 ) it follows by (3) that the volume of the solid is V = ! 2 0 A(x) dx = ! 2 0 π x4 + 2x2_x000b_ dx = π 1 5 x5 + 2 3 x3 _x0010_2 0 = 176π 15

discrepancies: The 2D washer at sample x is drawn as a full front-facing circle, whereas the source shows it as a thin vertical ellipse (a ring perpendicular to the x-axis seen in perspective)
The volume formula label 'V = ∫₀² π[(x²+1)² − 1²] dx = 206π/15' is an addition not present in the source figure

The solid of revolution in the source is an opaque shaded trumpet-like form with a visible cylindrical hole; the generated version is a faint translucent wireframe-looking mesh where the inner hole is hard to see
The rotation arrow in the source sits between the diagram and the solid on the axis; the generated arc arrow is small and hard to read
Source x-axis is plain with only ticks 0 and 2; generated axes and ticks are fine but the y-axis tick '4' and curve labeling 'x²' are placed less cleanly than the source

action_items: Orient the 2D washer ring perpendicular to the x-axis (thin vertical ellipse look) instead of facing the camera
Make the solid more opaque and reduce/remove the wireframe overlay so the shape and inner cylindrical hole read clearly like the source
Remove or shrink the 'V = ∫...' formula label since it does not appear in the source figure
Enlarge the rotation arrow so it is clearly visible on the axis between the diagram and the solid
